title: Caramel Apple Dutch Baby
changes_from_base: Butter melted in the pan in the oven, a spiced brown-sugar batter, and a skillet topping of apples simmered in a butter, cream and brown sugar caramel piled on instead of fresh berries.
summary: A cinnamon-spiced Dutch pancake crowned with apples cooked down into a rich, glossy caramel sauce.
equipment: 25 cm cast-iron or ovenproof frying pan

ingredients.item: fine sea salt or table salt
firm baking apples (about 3, such as Granny Smith, Gala or Jonagold), peeled, cored and cut into 2.5 cm slices
fine sea salt or table salt

steps.title: Heat Pan
steps.text: Preheat a 25 cm cast-iron or ovenproof frying pan in a 220 °C (200 °C fan) oven, add 55 g unsalted butter and leave 2-3 minutes to melt.

steps.title: Mix Batter
steps.text: Whisk together 3 large eggs, 95 g plain flour, 160 ml whole milk, 3 tbsp dark brown sugar, 1 tsp vanilla, ¾ tsp ground cinnamon, ½ tsp fine salt and ¼ tsp ground nutmeg in a large bowl until smooth.

steps.title: Bake
steps.text: Pour the batter into the hot buttered pan and bake 20-25 minutes until puffed at the edges and deep golden.

steps.title: Caramel Apples
steps.text: While the pancake bakes, melt 28 g unsalted butter in a separate frying pan over medium heat, stir in 60 ml double cream and 110 g dark brown sugar, add 450 g firm baking apples (peeled, cored and sliced into 2.5 cm pieces) and cook, stirring often, 8-10 minutes until the caramel thickens and apples soften; finish by stirring in ¾ tsp vanilla, ⅛ tsp cinnamon and ⅛ tsp salt.

steps.title: Plate
steps.text: Slide the warm pancake onto a plate, pile the caramel apples on top, slice into wedges and serve with whipped cream or ice cream if you like.

tips: Slice the apples to uniform thickness so they cook evenly in the caramel
Make the apple topping whilst the pancake bakes so everything finishes together
Serve straight away whilst the contrast between warm caramel and fluffy pancake is at its peak
storage: Serve warm. Cool leftovers in a shallow container and refrigerate within 2 hours (within 1 hour on a day above 32°C).
